subject: Successive passes of the loop surveyed as profiles stacked back in depth, the pass playing now in front and older, fresher passes receding behind it with chainage along the front.
controls: wear: each profile is a little more eroded than the one behind it, so the stack goes from crisp at the back to rounded at the front (shape; only the front profile is a mutable outline, older ones are re-keyed when a pass ages).
wow: the passes shear sideways against each other along the tape, up to 10 px each (position of each layer).
length: the spacing between passes opens from 12 to 26 px, so a longer loop pushes history further back (position along the stack).
bias: the front profile's level, 1.3x under-biased to 0.7x over-biased (scale of the front layer).
risks: At defaults (wear 0) all five profiles are identical, so the rest frame shows only a stack, and the history this subject exists for appears only once wear is up and a note has run. Bias scale spans 1.86x but scaling a node also scales its stroke, so the front line thickens past 2.5 px at the under-bias end; bias may need shape instead, which collides with wear on the same part. Wow as shear at 10 px is under the 24 px floor at 1:1 and needs more travel. Re-keying all five profiles each pass is 5 path redraws per loop period; at 0.05 s loops that is too often, so the stack should advance by moving nodes, not rewriting them.
